whaleWisdomChecks.note: Rendered profile checked. Two put rows use underlying-share values, not premiums. Dataroma excludes those rows. Different scopes change portfolio weights.

insights.title: Technology managers did not move together
insights.fact: Tiger Global's reported quantities declined approximately 45.39% for Alphabet Class A, 12.29% for TSMC, 8.54% for Meta, 6.77% for Nvidia and 3.16% for Amazon versus March.
insights.interpretation: This contrasts with Appaloosa's increases in Amazon, Meta and TSMC. It does not support a unanimous technology-buying narrative.
insights.watch: Compare earnings and valuation stock by stock; manager motives and current October positions are unknown.

insights.title: Quality-oriented ownership can coexist with reductions
insights.fact: Akre's reported quantities declined approximately 32.21% for Visa, 28.82% for Brookfield, 25.85% for KKR and 12.77% for Mastercard versus March.
insights.interpretation: A large existing holding does not establish ongoing accumulation. These are reported quantity changes, not a confirmed explanation of why the positions changed.
insights.watch: Distinguish existing concentration from additions; do not translate a reduction into a short recommendation.

insights.title: Selective China exposure and a critical options distinction
insights.fact: Appaloosa's reported Baidu quantity increased approximately 87.11%, while Alibaba declined 42.28%. Apple and Berkshire entries in the June table are puts, not ordinary long stock positions.
insights.interpretation: A blanket China exit or a headline that Appaloosa bought Apple stock would misdescribe the filing. Option underlying-share value is not the premium paid.
insights.watch: Review security type, share-count changes and the portfolio-value denominator before drawing a conclusion.
